title: Amemiya 2017 foot-sole vibration PPS
citation: Amemiya, T., Ikei, Y., Hirota, K., & Kitazaki, M. (2017). Vibration on the soles of the feet evoking a sensation of walking expands peripersonal space. 2017 IEEE World Haptics Conference (WHC), 605–610.
notes: Design inspection for the 192 conditioning trials in six condition-specific blocks. Original sound, independently synchronized heel and chest outputs, and study-specific response capture are still required for a participant session.

auditory_stimulus.signal: Amplitude-modulated white noise simulating a virtual approaching source
auditory_stimulus.gain_law_ambiguity: The prose and Fig. 2 describe a rising level during approach. The same paragraph says the level decreased 6 dB when distance halved. The delivered gain law remains unresolved.

timing_evidence.main_trial_prose_anchor: Sound onset (§III.C), without an explicit signed schedule.
timing_evidence.main_trial_figure_anchor: The dashed marks in Fig. 2 show a time interval from chest pulse to sound offset.
timing_evidence.preview_derivation: Subtract the printed interval magnitudes from Fig. 2's drawn 5000 ms audio window. This gives 3860 ms for the illustrated 80 cm probe, close to the waveform's approximately 3856 ms onset.
timing_evidence.control_scope: Fig. 2 and §III.C differ on timing reference. The preview offsets implement the figure interpretation. Verify on the original task before participant use.

preview_equivalence.audio: Generated 5 s, 44.1 kHz, fixed-gain continuous white noise for software timing. These files are preview assets; the reported perceived approach and dB(A) envelope require original or validated calibrated audio.
preview_equivalence.trajectory: Path-length and propagation-speed fields provide the five-second render duration. The paper's 0.7 m/s and nominal probe distances are retained as separate study evidence.
preview_equivalence.target: Any generated Toolkit tactile cue is a software marker for verifying schedule offsets. The Acouve drive waveform and delivery latency require external validation.
preview_equivalence.schedule: The preview uses one illustrative ABCCBA assignment and eight repeats per distance in each block. Each pattern occurs in two blocks, giving the reported 16 repeats per distance and 192 total trials. Realized block assignments, per-block frequency and trial order are unknown.

heel_conditioning.apparatus: Acouve Lab Vp416 voice coils attached to slippers

conditions.label: Walking-sound vibration
conditions.reported_signal: Recorded footsteps, low-pass filtered at 120 Hz

conditions.label: Asynchronous walking-sound vibration
conditions.reported_signal: Same recording, with each step onset asynchronized and randomized each trial

conditions.label: 60 Hz sinusoidal vibration
conditions.reported_signal: 60 Hz sine, with the same step-onset schedule as the walking-sound condition

heel_conditioning.reported_amplitude_matching: Matched average amplitudes across the three patterns
heel_conditioning.rhythmic_figure_example: Fig. 1A shows approximately 600 ms between alternating visible footstep bursts and 1200 ms on the same heel. This measures an illustrated example.

chest_target.apparatus: Acouve Lab Vp216 voice coil on an adjustable neckstrap
chest_target.figure_scope: The written Methods and Fig. 2 annotation give 150 Hz and 200 ms. The illustrated trace yields about 200 Hz and 100 ms. Delivered values require verification.

reported_trial_schedule.condition_block_order: Modified Latin square across participants with reversal within participant (ABCCBA).

baseline.response: Detect the chest pulse as quickly as possible with no sound and no heel vibration.

response_and_analysis.task: Press on the numeric keyboard as quickly as possible to detect the chest pulse while seated and holding the head still. Ignore the auditory stimulus.
response_and_analysis.primary_analysis: Use reciprocal reaction times for the repeated-measures heel-pattern × distance ANOVA. The Fig. 4 response summaries are RT differences from the tactile-only baseline.
response_and_analysis.boundary_definition: Farthest tested distance with significant facilitation in the one-sided paired tests versus tactile-only baseline.

after_main_subjective_walking_control.scope: Seven main-task participants performed both controls afterward. The two control orders were counterbalanced in the reported design.
after_main_subjective_walking_control.scale: Seven-point agreement that the participant felt as if walking.
after_main_subjective_walking_control.response_device: Numeric keyboard held with the right hand

implemented_controls: Six condition-locked blocks × four probe distances × eight preview repeats reproduce the 192 conditioning trials under a symmetric split.
implementation_gaps: Original 2017 white-noise audio, sample format, dose calibration and author-confirmed magnitude law.
Independent synchronized bilateral heel and chest actuator scheduler, Acouve drive files, measured amplitude and verified tactile timing.
Original participant-to-order assignments, per-block distance counts, rest realization and numeric key capture.
Exact sound/chest timing anchor resolution, tactile-only baseline allocation and any catch trials or ITI schedule.
